panels.description: Most recent cold-lookup latency. Healthy ~100ms. ~2.4s is the signature of the router<->NAS BIND forwarding loop (fixed 2026-05-22) — a recurrence shows up here first.
panels.title: Cold Latency — Forwarding-Loop Detector

panels.description: Most recent warm (cache-hit) latency. Near-zero when healthy. If warm is ALSO slow, the problem is upstream/transport, not the router's cold-cache path.
panels.title: Warm Latency (cache-hit)

panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape the DNS probe on the NAS.
panels.title: DNS Probe Exporter Reachable
DNS layer state — Router vs NAS BIND (wedge = Router DOWN / BIND UP)
panels.description: Fast ~45s dual-probe. Router DOWN while BIND UP = router DNS wedge (reboot Google Wifi). Both DOWN = NAS BIND down (fix DSM DNSServer; do NOT reboot router).

panels.title: Fast-probe latency — Router vs NAS BIND (alert > 300ms / 10m)
panels.description: Per-layer fast-probe latency. Sustained rise above the ~40ms p95 baseline is pre-wedge degradation; multi-second spikes on BIND can signal a forwarding loop. 3000ms = a probe timeout.

panels.title: Fast-probe failure rate — the wedge canary (alert > 5 / 15m)
panels.description: rate of intermittent fast-probe timeouts that recover. A climbing router rate is the leading indicator of a hard wedge (the 2026-06-28 outage followed a brief upstream stall).

panels.title: Router uptime (24h)
panels.description: Fraction of the last 24h the router DNS probe was up.
